transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
After meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in China this week, President Trump
is defending calling him a friend.
Trump claims that Putin would love to end the Ukraine war, even though Putin continues
attacks nearly five years after his forces invaded.
NPR's Franco Ordonez has more.
Trump was asked today if Putin, who he called his friend, was also America's friend.
I can't speak to America.
He really couldn't answer that, but he did continue to make the case that his relationship
with Putin would reap benefits for America, though we haven't really seen that yet.
The war in Ukraine continues to rage on, but we are seeing allies start to build alliances
with other nations as confidence in the U.S. falters and they look to reduce their dependence
on the U.S.
And NPR's Franco Ordonez is reporting.
Tech stocks dragged down markets this week.
NPR's Stephen Besaha reports the tech-heavy Nasdaq wiped out its gains for the year.
There was plenty of positive news from artificial intelligence companies this week.
Invidia reported earnings that easily beat Wall Street expectations, and Enthropic had
a record-setting public offering Thursday.
None of that stopped a rough end of the week on the market.
Envidia's stock continued its nosedive, down about 12 percent for the day.
Tech stock fell close to 10 percent.
All that signals that investors are expecting an AI slowdown.
One positive sign for a Thanksgiving traveler is looking to drive rather than fly next week.
The national average for a gallon of gas is down to $3.68, according to AAA, a drop of
about 50 cents from the start of November.
Stephen Besaha, NPR News, Birmingham, Alabama.
The Department of Energy has officially secured the money it needs to move its staff into
the Department of Education building.
NPR's Janaki Mehta reports this is more than just Washington bureaucracy and logistics.
It's also part of the dismantling of the education department.
Education Secretary Linda McMahon has spent her tenure doing what she was hired to do,
breaking up her agency.
Half the staff were cut last year, and hundreds of remaining employees have been scattered
across Washington.
While the timeline for the actual move isn't clear, the plan to shift energy department
workers into the headquarters of the Ed Department puts a nail in the coffin, cementing a physical
dismantling of the agency.
The historic education building was named for Lyndon B. Johnson, the former president
and school teacher who made education programs, like helping low-income students, central
to his agenda.
Janaki Mehta, NPR News.
A federal appeals court has granted a request by environmentalists to put on hold a permit
that cleared the way for the Army to detonate several tons of bomb-making chemicals in Iowa.
The ruling puts in jeopardy the military's plans to deal with dozens of barrels of lead
azide pending further direction by the court.
The Army has said the chemicals are unstable and the risk of explosion is growing, particularly
as temperatures drop.
The detonation was initially planned for today.
This is NPR News from Washington.
New York City Mayor Zoran Mamdani says he plans to shutter the notorious Rikers Island
jail complex by 2032.
It comes as the city is all but certain to blow past a legal requirement to close Rikers
and replace it with four smaller, more modern jails by 2027.
Rikers Island has symbolized dysfunction in the city's criminal justice system for years.
A judge has appointed an outside manager to restore order and implement reforms.
Colorado has declared its second major disaster this month after catastrophic flooding, from
member station KSUT Adam Burke reports.
Repeated flooding in the Four Corners region destroyed roads, bridges and critical infrastructure
and displaced thousands of residents in its formal request to the White House, Colorado
put preliminary reconstruction cost estimates for public infrastructure at $28.5 million.
The state expects those numbers to increase.
Governor Jared Polis says the Trump administration has not responded to the state's first $27
million request delivered on October 31st.
We hope that nobody plays politics with the lives of real people, many of whom lost their
homes.
They impacted New Mexico, Arizona, Utah and tribal nations as well.
Recovery cost estimates have grown to the hundreds of millions of dollars.
For NPR News, I'm Adam Burke in Durango.
Grand Theft Auto 6 set a record with $3.79 billion in first day retail sales yesterday.
Video game maker Rockstar said it sold 32.5 million units pre-release, setting a record
across platforms, the standard edition of the game retails for around $80.
This is NPR News from Washington.

topics.text: Trump defends calling Putin a friend, saying Putin would love to end Ukraine war
Tech stocks drag markets down, Nasdaq erases its gains for the year amid AI slowdown fears
Gas prices fall to $3.68 a gallon nationally, a 50-cent drop since early November
Energy Department secures funding to move staff into Education Department building, advancing agency dismantling
Federal appeals court pauses Army permit to detonate lead azide chemicals in Iowa
NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani pledges to close Rikers Island jail complex by 2032
Colorado declares second major disaster this month after catastrophic Four Corners flooding
Grand Theft Auto 6 sets record with $3.79 billion in first-day retail sales
